Since validations check for non-overlap of any of these network types, this can only be accomplished by settting a non-default value for {{internalJoinSubnet}} in the install-config. items.toString:
Sometimes users want to use the default {{internalJoinSubnet}} for OVNk ({{100.64.0.0/16}}) for other purposes (in the cluster/service/machine networks). Since validations check for non-overlap of any of these network types, this can only be accomplished by settting a non-default value for {{internalJoinSubnet}} in the install-config. This is possible in the installer since [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CORS-2753|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CORS-2753|smart-link].

However, in ABI this field is (silently) ignored. Furthermore, the field is missing from assisted-service’s definition of an install-config, so the user can’t add it to the install config overrides either.

Unfortunately there will still be no way to both reuse the default {{internalJoinSubnet}} elsewhere and also override other fields from {{openshift/cluster-network-03-config.yml}} (such as e.g. {{internalTransitSwitchSubnet}}). If {{internalJoinSubnet}} is not set in the install-config, the installer (when run by assisted-service to generate the ignition) will not generate that manifest and the user is free to supply their own to override it. However, if the value is set to something other than the default, the installer will generate the manifest and any attempt by the user to supply their own manifest will be blocked as described in [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AGENT-653|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AGENT-653|smart-link].

The update-hosts service is currently injected via the [BootstrapIgnition asset|https://github.com/openshift/appliance/blob/869d350f11e7c15777945ad2116aa32fedb13793/pkg/asset/ignition/bootstrap_ignition.go#L62]. The main task oc the [update-host |https://github.com/openshift/appliance/blob/869d350f11e7c15777945ad2116aa32fedb13793/data/scripts/bin/update-hosts.sh.template#L32]script is to inject an host ignition (that will be applied on first reboot) for adding a bunch of additional services.

Given that any host configuration should be orchestrated only by the MCO IRI controller, keeping this isolated / not-synchronized point of configuration may be fragile and potentially cause issues, so it’d better to avoid it all in the interactive workflow (live ISO).

Also the ignition adds some services that are not used in the interactive workflow (to be reviewed, but almost none of them should be really required; if so, they should be moved somewhere else).

The only step which should be kept (and properly refactored ) is the support for adding [ABI extra manifests|https://github.com/openshift/appliance/blob/869d350f11e7c15777945ad2116aa32fedb13793/data/scripts/bin/update-hosts.sh.template#L48-L59]. A proper analysis will be required to decide where to move this part.
